text.p: Prices of both industrial and precious metals moved higher on Wednesday as the mood of gloom and doom which prevailed earlier in the week lifted slightly. Explaining gold's price bounce amid a month-old downtrend, one dealer said: "It's been too bearish to be true recently and when everyone's bearish, it tends to go the other way."
Gold closed at $380.60 an ounce in London, compared to $378.65 on Tuesday. In New York, gold was quoted at $379.70.
Copper led the way in the industrial metals sector.
But wheat prices fell sharply in Chicago while oil slipped slightly in New York.

Copper settled at firmer levels on Wednesday afternoon after being whipped around over the past few days, leaving some traders confounded about future direction. Three months prices stabilised above the $1,900-a-tonne benchmark in thin London Metal Exchange (LME) afternoon trade after shooting to nearly $2,000 last Friday and slumping to $1,875 in inter-office business late on Tuesday.
Last business on Wednesday's kerb was at $1,918, up $28 from Tuesday and just off a high of $1,922.
"I'm standing aside at the moment. I just can't get a handle on the market," one floor trader said.
Volumes have been mostly lacklustre recently as traders struggle to figure out whether much Sumitomo material is still overhanging the market and how the fundamentals will pan out.
"There was one 100-lot deal yesterday, but mostly we've been seeing eight or nine lots at a go these days," a trader said.

The other metals largely followed copper higher after Tuesday's rout, but aluminium remained trapped below $1,400. Aluminium recovered from a fresh 2-1/4 year low on Tuesday, finishing $9.50 firmer at $1,377.
Nickel also managed a healthy bounce, probing the $7,100 barrier on the kerb and ending $90 higher at $7,095 after retesting the downside earlier in the day, bottoming at $6,970.

Lead ended at $760, up $3 from the previous close and well off Tuesday's nadir of $745. Zinc, which has remained a pillar of stability while the others flopped about, finished the kerb at $1,021, up $2 and well within the range of the past week.

New York precious metals futures ended higher for a second day on Wednesday but the month long downtrend is not seen broken yet, dealers said. COMEX December gold ended up US$1.30 an ounce at US$382.30 after trading in a range of $380.60-383.30. In bullion trade, gold was quoted at $379.70 compared with London's afternoon fix of $380.30 and the New York close on Tuesday of about $378.60.
Wheat prices fell sharply in Chicago on a rumour that Egypt had rejected a cargo of U.S. wheat. Prices closed two to 11-1/4 cents lower with December down 11-1/4 at US$4.22-1/2.

November crude settled at US$24.05 a barrel, down nine cents. Heating oil rose on an unexpected draw in historically low distillate inventories while curde was caught in the downdraft created by gasoline's slippage.
